title: Pork and Pickle Pie
subtitle: A raised shortcrust pork pie with a layer of tangy pickle
excerpt: Seasoned pork mince packed into a deep shortcrust case with a sharp pickle layer through the centre. Best eaten cold the day after baking.
sourceNotes: British pork pie tradition with a pickle layer, drawing on Northern raised pie methods and picnic pie conventions.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the fully baked and chilled pie whole. Defrost overnight in the fridge before slicing.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake the day before and refrigerate overnight. The flavour and texture improve after resting cold.

content.text: This is a deep-filled cold pie of pork mince with a stripe of pickle through the middle. It slices cleanly when properly chilled. Eat it the next day; the texture is firmer and the flavour better after an overnight rest in the fridge.

items.prepNote: two thirds base and sides, one third lid

content.text: Mix the pork mince, chopped bacon, grated onion, sage, mustard powder, salt and pepper in a large bowl. Combine thoroughly with your hands.
Heat the oven to 200C. Roll out two thirds of the pastry and line the deep pie dish, pressing it firmly into the sides. Leave a little overhang.
Press half the pork mixture into the base, levelling it firmly. Spread the pickle evenly over the pork layer.
Press the remaining pork mixture over the pickle, levelling it flat. It should sit just below the pastry rim.
Roll the remaining pastry for the lid. Brush the rim with beaten egg. Place the lid on top and press the edges firmly together. Trim and crimp. Cut two slits in the top.
Brush all over with beaten egg. Bake for 60 minutes until the pastry is deep gold. Cover with foil after 40 minutes if the top is browning too fast.
Cool fully in the tin, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours before slicing. Overnight is better.

items.cause: It was cut while still warm, or it was not chilled long enough.
items.fix: Always chill the pie for a minimum of 2 hours. Overnight gives the cleanest slices.

items.cause: The pork filling released too much liquid during baking.
items.fix: Drain any visible liquid from the filling before the lid goes on. Bake on a preheated baking tray for a crisper base.

items.symptom: The top browns before the pork is cooked.
items.fix: Cover loosely with foil from the 40-minute mark and check the internal temperature. Pork needs to reach 75C.
